question.worked_solution:
The denominator is $3+10\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $3-10\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $3-10\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{3+10\text{i}} & =\frac{6}{3+10\text{i}}\cdot \frac{3-10\text{i}}{3-10\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{18-60\text{i}}{9-30\text{i}+30\text{i}-{10}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{18-60\text{i}}{9-100{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{18-60\text{i}}{9-100(-1)} \\  & =\frac{18-60\text{i}}{9+100} \\  & =\frac{18-60\text{i}}{109}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{18-60\text{i}}{109}=\frac{18}{109}-\frac{60}{109}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
